package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5 (and others during the attack window)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised to include the SUNBURST backdoor, which enabled covert remote code execution and data exfiltration by attackers. The malicious code was inserted into the official, code-signed SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll and distributed as a legitimate update, allowing attackers to gain persistent access to customer environments.

execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (malicious code injected into main application binary)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after update installation, the code checks for network connectivity and anti-analysis conditions, then initiates a beacon to a remote C2 server, receives attacker commands, executes those commands, and exfiltrates data from the environment, resulting in covert remote control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes unauthorized outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains, performs anti-analysis checks to evade detection, receives and executes arbitrary remote commands, and exfiltrates sensitive data. These behaviors are not present in legitimate SolarWinds Orion DLLs and are characteristic of advanced persistent threat backdoors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate update DLLs should not initiate outbound network connections to unknown or non-SolarWinds domains, should not execute arbitrary code received from external sources, and should not exfiltrate internal data. The presence of anti-analysis logic further violates expectations for normal update behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate Orion DLLs may contact SolarWinds servers for telemetry or update checks, but they do not execute arbitrary remote commands or exfiltrate sensitive data to non-SolarWinds domains. Any network activity should be limited to known, documented vendor endpoints and should not include anti-analysis or evasion logic.
key_indicators: Outbound network connections from SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll to non-SolarWinds domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Conditional execution based on anti-analysis or sandbox detection
Ability to receive and execute arbitrary commands from remote C2 servers
Data exfiltration routines embedded within the DLL
Presence of code sections not found in legitimate versions of the DLL

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll and the DLL is code-signed as part of an official SolarWinds update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of the compromised update to customer environments

attack_chain.action: Customers install the signed update, loading the malicious SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll into their Orion platform.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code within trusted customer environments

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the SUNBURST backdoor activates, performs anti-analysis checks, establishes covert C2 communications, and awaits attacker instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote command execution and exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from SolarWinds Orion processes to non-SolarWinds domains
Presence of code sections in SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll not found in legitimate versions
Runtime anti-analysis or sandbox evasion checks within the DLL
Execution of arbitrary commands received from external servers by the Orion process
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with hash values differing from known-good versions
Code-signed DLLs containing unknown or suspicious code sections not present in official releases
network_indicators: Connections from Orion servers to known SUNBURST C2 domains such as avsvmcloud.com
Beaconing patterns from SolarWinds Orion processes to external IPs or domains not associated with SolarWinds
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound network activity from SolarWinds Orion processes, especially to domains such as avsvmcloud.com. Verify the integrity and hash of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll against known-good versions. Inspect DLLs for the presence of code sections implementing C2 communication, anti-analysis logic, or remote command execution. Alert on code-signed updates that introduce new or undocumented network behaviors or anti-analysis routines.
